Cross-border network (international links): purpose is “Connecting the service centers to the worldwide internet”; typical distance >1,000 km. Technologies shown include WWW, terrestrial fiber, and subsea cable. Middle-mile network (distribution): purpose is “Connecting bigger cities together and routing data to the service centers”; typical distance 10–1,000 km. The diagram shows fiber-optic backbone/fiber, an IXP, a colocation data center, fiber or microwave backbone, and a satellite link connected through an earth station. Last mile (access): purpose is “Distributing internet from the middle mile in the community to individual homes and businesses”; typical distance <1–5 km. Technologies shown include fiber, DSL, coaxial, cellular towers, wireless (Wi-Fi, LTE, TV white space), satellite link (DTH), and balloons and drones. The network paths visually connect international links to middle-mile infrastructure and then to household/business endpoints; satellite and wireless routes also connect to last-mile endpoints. Source: Adapted from World Bank (2019c).
